title: Length identity under coordinate restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $f_b$ be the restriction of $f$ to last coordinate $b$, let $D_i$ denote the coordinate half-difference, and let $U$ be the Gaussian profile equal to $\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$ and zero otherwise. Then the Euclidean length formed from $U(f_b(x))$, the derivatives $D_i f_b(x)$ for $i<n$, and the half-difference $(f_0(x)-f_1(x))/2$ equals the Euclidean length formed from $U(f(x,b))$ and all derivatives $D_i f(x,b)$ for $i<n+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n+1$
$x$ is in the Boolean cube of dimension $n$
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, and $d=(f_0-f_1)/2$. For every $b\in\{0,1\}$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, $\sqrt{(\sqrt{\overline I(f_b(x))^2+\sum_{i<n}(D_i f_b(x))^2})^2+d(x)^2}=\sqrt{\overline I(f(x,b))^2+\sum_{i<n+1}(D_i f(x,b))^2}$, where $D_i$ denotes the coordinate half-difference.
